content.text:
I've submitted **index 88** (Bi 0.08, Cu 0.50, V 0.42) as the best composition. At 2.5e-7 A it had the highest photocurrent of the three I measured. That was the whole merit budget. I didn't use any of the 5 XRD measurements, so which phases are present is inferred from composition alone.

**Why I looked there:** the light is 2.06 eV, which is too low in energy for BiVO4 to absorb (its bandgap is about 2.4 eV). Copper vanadates such as Cu2V2O7 and Cu3V2O8 have bandgaps of about 1.9–2.0 eV, so I spent the measurements on compositions with little Bi that are rich in Cu and V.

| Index | Composition (Bi / Cu / V) | Photocurrent | Region |
|---|---|---|---|
| 88 | 0.08 / 0.50 / 0.42 | 2.5e-7 A | Cu:V ≈ 1:1, near Cu2V2O7 |
| 56 | 0.08 / 0.61 / 0.32 | 1.8e-7 A | more Cu-rich, near Cu3V2O8 |
| 3 | 0.36 / 0.21 / 0.43 | 8e-8 A | Bi- and V-rich, BiVO4-like |

With only three data points out of 188 candidates, there's no guarantee index 88 is the best in the library. Compositions near it, such as 113, 95 and 70, are untested and could score higher.
